sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Only by doing this can Singapore survive and continue to be successful; only by doing this can our children enjoy a peaceful, prosperous and equal society, generation after generation.

sections.label: Constitutional Commission and White Paper
sections.summary: A nine-member Constitutional Commission appointed in February reviewed three aspects of the Elected Presidency, and the Government issued a White Paper in September responding to its report.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A nine-member Constitutional Commission was appointed by the Prime Minister earlier this year in February to review three aspects of the Elected Presidency.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Upon the release of the Commission's report, the Government has subsequently in September issued a White Paper in response to the Constitutional Commission's report.

sections.label: Public awareness of issue
sections.summary: Data shows rising public awareness from June to October 2016, though about 37% polled still do not follow the issue.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Although the data shows that there was an increasing awareness by the public since June 2016 to October 2016, about 37% of those polled are still not following the issue.

sections.label: Raising private sector threshold
sections.summary: Recommendations include raising the threshold for private sector candidates from $100 million paid-up capital to $500 million shareholders' equity.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, the recommendations include raising the threshold for private sector candidates from senior executives of companies with $100 million in paid-up capital to $500 million in shareholders' equity.

sections.label: Endorsements and non-partisan Presidency
sections.summary: It asks whether political bodies may endorse presidential candidates, whether that defeats non-partisanship, and whether the model works under coalition government.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Should the political bodies/figures be allowed to endorse presidential candidates?

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If they are to be truly non-partisan, would not allowing them to be endorsed defeat the essence of non-partisan spirit?

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hypothetically, what if we have a coalition government?

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will this model of Elected Presidency and CPA still work?

sections.label: Minority representation in Presidency
sections.summary: The speaker feels ensuring minority representation in the Presidency is the most important of all proposed amendments.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Of all the proposed amendments, I feel that the most important is ensuring minority representation in the Presidency.

sections.label: Malay President minority representation
sections.summary: It notes 46 years since the last Malay President, Yusof Ishak, and supports the amendment ensuring minority representation in the Presidency.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Our last Malay President was our first President, Mr Yusof Ishak who held this highest office from 1965 to 1970.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: In other words, it has been 46 years since we last had a President from the Malay race.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: If we agree that the President is a symbol of unity and the personification of the state, then the proposed amendment to ensure minority representation in the Presidency is a timely and long overdue move that I strongly support.

sections.label: Reviewing qualifying criteria periodically
sections.summary: The speaker supports periodic review of qualifying criteria, noting the recommended criteria seemed to restrict eligibility to CEOs and senior management.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: To be relevant with time and context, I agree and support that the qualifying criteria must be reviewed on a periodic basis, especially this case in point pertaining to the post that belongs to the highest office in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Based on the recommended criteria, the initial impression was that the stringent criteria would have restricted the eligible candidates to individuals who have experience as CEOs and also senior management in the private or public sector.

sections.label: Criteria for elected President
sections.summary: Stringent criteria ensure a qualified individual with critical capabilities for crises and safeguarding past Reserves, with possible broadening over time.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The stringent criteria recommended are necessary to ensure that we have the best qualified individual with critical capabilities to make central decisions when crises arise and safeguard our past Reserves for future generation.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: In order to achieve a right balance between both roles, and the diversity and inclusiveness of different individuals who can potentially be our Head of State, we can consider broadening the criteria over time and supplementing it by reviewing the process and selection of the CPA.

sections.label: Future elections without reserved election
sections.summary: Elections should let any capable person regardless of race vie for the highest office, making the term reserved election unnecessary.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Elections by then should be one where any capable man or woman, regardless of their race, will feel confident and comfortable to step forward and vie for the highest office on this land.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: By then, the term "reserved election" would be unnecessary.

sections.label: President's ceremonial and custodial roles
sections.summary: The President must be equally qualified to deliver both the ceremonial and custodial roles.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Among the two roles that the President is accountable for, he or she must be equally qualified to deliver both the ceremonial and custodial roles.

sections.label: Qualities needed in President
sections.summary: The individual must understand a different role, demonstrate independent thought for national interest, and reconcile differences with Government to preserve wealth.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Rather, it is the need for this individual to: (a) understand their role as one being different from what they used to contribute when in governance; (b) establish their role in a needful manner and consciously demonstrate independence of thoughts with the nation's interest as top priority; and (c) to demonstrate the ability to reconcile differences in opinions and work through solutions with the Government to ensure that all the key proposition is in preserving wealth for the future generations of Singapore.

sections.label: Senior executive and equity criteria
sections.summary: Two changes are that only the most senior executive can be a candidate and minimum shareholders' equity of S$500 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Two significant changes which I would like to highlight are: only the most senior executive, however named, can be allowed as a candidate; and minimum shareholders' equity of S$500 million.

sections.label: Widening most senior executive notion
sections.summary: The speaker urges reconsidering widening the notion of most senior executive to include CFO and COO within that framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Henceforth, I urge that we re-consider widening the notion of the most senior executive to include those whom I have mentioned, like the CFO and COO, to be considered, too, within this "most senior executive" framework.

sections.label: Minority community highest office
sections.summary: A minority-community member appreciates the Commission for ensuring a minority member will always have a place in Singapore's highest office.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As a member coming from a minority community, I would like to express my appreciation to the Commission for having included this in ensuring that a member from the minority community will always have a place in the highest office in Singapore.

sections.label: Reserved Presidential Election for Malays
sections.summary: The speaker supports a five-term hiatus provision, with next year's Presidential Election reserved for Malays after 46 years without a Malay President.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As a proponent of affirmative action and without compromising our principles of meritocracy, I fully support this provision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For the first time, a provision for a five-term hiatus, which was suggested by the Constitutional Commission, and also supported by the Government, will commence at the next Presidential Election, as proposed by the Prime Minister yesterday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister also said, the Presidential Election next year will be reserved for Malays, after 46 years without someone from the Malay community assuming the office of the President.

sections.label: Minority President every five terms
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a minority President can assume office only once every five terms, with the provision reconsidered if no minority President in five terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Does this mean that a President from the minority group, including Malays, can only assume the office of the Elected President once every five terms?

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If elected, this provision will only be reconsidered, if there are no Presidents from the minority group in the next five terms.

sections.label: Candidate character and competence criteria
sections.summary: The speaker reminds that clause 19(20)(e) requires the Presidential Elections Committee to assess integrity, good character and reputation, and that stringent criteria of character and competence are needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In doing so, to some extent, the qualification criteria that were set out in the Constitution on the character of the candidate have not been given as much attention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I would just like to remind everyone that clause 19(20)(e) of our Constitution outlines that the Presidential Elections Committee, before issuing certificate of eligibility, is to assess that the candidate is a person of integrity, good character and reputation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The eligibility criteria must lend weight to both the character and competence of the candidates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: While many will agree on the need for high standards and the quality of the candidates, and the concerns that perhaps the criteria being too stringent might limit the pool of individuals that can qualify, but I would like to remind everyone that, given the significance of the role of the Elected President and what he or she will play, we do need stringent criteria.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Not that we do not trust our GP, we do.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But there are specific skills that are still required and, therefore, the need for the stringent criteria, both of character and of technical competence, that are required.

sections.label: Inclusive highest office representation
sections.summary: The amendments aim to ensure the highest office is inclusive and represents the main communities of Chinese, Malay, Indian and Eurasian in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: We do, however, need to be able to speak about how we can ensure that the highest office in this country is inclusive and that no racial group in a multiracial Singapore feels that they are not able to achieve it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It is in this spirit that the amendments are made to ensure representation of the main communities of Chinese, Malay, Indian and Eurasian in Singapore for the Office of the President.

sections.label: Reserved election and women representation
sections.summary: A reserved election opens to all races if no qualified candidate from that racial group exists, and the speaker asks about women, who make up 51% of Singapore's population.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: If during the reserved election, there is no qualified candidate from that racial group, the election will then be opened to candidates from all races." It is important to note that a reserved election will not be required if the election produces Presidents of different races.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It is only if no persons belonging to one of the main racial communities has held the office of President for a five-term hiatus, which translates to 30 years, that there will be a reserved election for that racial group.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: And in the last 46 years, we have not seen a Malay candidate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: As I reviewed the amendment and so on – this is not so much related to race – I could not help but ask this question: what about women?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I am not advocating for provisions in the Constitution to be made for women representation, but we must, however, recognise that women do make up 51% of Singapore's population.

sections.label: Independent Constitutional Commission recommendations
sections.summary: The Bill's changes follow recommendations from an independent Constitutional Commission appointed by the Prime Minister in January, which consulted widely and reviewed in a non-partisan, inclusive, transparent, open and comprehensive manner.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The changes proposed in the Bill flow from the recommendations of an independent Constitutional Commission appointed by the Prime Minister in January this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: There was wide consultation by the independent Commission, which conducted its review in a non-partisan, inclusive, transparent, open and comprehensive manner.

sections.label: Proposed elected Upper House
sections.summary: Their proposal for an Upper House composed of elected Senators is a fundamental change to our institutions of government.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Their proposal for an Upper House – composed of elected Senators – is a fundamental change to our institutions of government.

sections.label: WP declined invitation
sections.summary: The WP was the only one of the 20 invited contributors that declined the invitation.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The WP was the only one of the 20 invited contributors that declined the invitation.

sections.label: Commission on unbundling Presidency functions
sections.summary: The Commission stated in paragraph 7.47 that unbundling the custodial and symbolic functions is a proposal the Government may wish to consider if and when appropriate and timely for a more fundamental change to the Presidency.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: In paragraph 7.47 of the report, the Commission stated, with regard to the proposal to unbundle the custodial and symbolic functions, and I quote, "The Commission considers that this is a proposal that the Government may wish to consider if and when it is appropriate and timely to undertake a more fundamental change to the Presidency".

sections.label: Commission's main recommendations on Elected Presidency
sections.summary: The Commission had described an appointed council of experts with no veto powers, but its main recommendations focused on enhancing the existing Elected Presidency, covering eligibility criteria, the CPA, and the hiatus-triggered mechanism for multiracial representation.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Furthermore, what the members of the Commission had actually described for consideration was an appointed council of experts with no veto powers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Instead, Mdm Speaker, the Commission's main recommendations focused squarely on enhancing and improving the existing institution of the Elected Presidency.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: It dealt with the revision of the eligibility criteria, the strengthening of the CPA, and the hiatus-triggered mechanism to ensure multiracial representation.

sections.label: Revised threshold and minority candidates
sections.summary: The Government accepted the Commission's recommendation to increase the quantitative threshold, with more companies meeting the revised $500 million shareholders' equity threshold than the 158 companies in 1993 meeting the $100 million paid-up capital threshold, and qualified minority candidates will continue from both sectors, though a precise figure is unavailable.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The Government has accepted the Commission's recommendation to increase the quantitative threshold.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: As I have already mentioned in my opening speech, there are significantly more companies today that would meet the revised threshold of $500 million shareholders' equity than the 158 companies in 1993, which would have met the $100 million paid-up capital threshold.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: There will continue to be qualified minority candidates, from both the public and private sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: A precise figure is not available – companies do not make public the information on the racial background of their officers.

sections.label: Uniform CPA consultation and overruling
sections.summary: The changes adopt a uniform approach to the President's obligation to consult the CPA and extend the overruling mechanism uniformly to these areas.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The changes merely adopt a uniform approach towards the President's obligation to consult the CPA on financial and appointment-related matters, as well as extend the overruling mechanism in a uniform way to these areas.

sections.label: Harmonising Parliamentary overruling framework
sections.summary: The approach harmonises Parliamentary overruling by subjecting the rest of the President's core custodial powers to the same overruling framework.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The approach taken is to harmonise the approach towards Parliamentary overruling by subjecting the rest of his core custodial powers to the same overruling framework.

sections.label: CPA advice and veto powers
sections.summary: The CPA advises the President, but the President decides on vetoes, and the CPA has no veto powers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: As for the weight given to the CPA's recommendations, I have already explained in my opening speech that the CPA's role is to provide its advice to the President.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: It is the President who decides whether to veto a Government proposal, and not the CPA.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The CPA has no veto powers, neither over what the President does nor what the Government proposes.

sections.label: Balancing accountability and confidentiality
sections.summary: The White Paper approach seeks to balance enhancing CPA and President accountability for veto matters with protecting sensitive and confidential information.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: As stated in the White Paper, the proposed approach seeks to strike a suitable balance between enhancing the CPA's and the President's accountability for matters involving vetoes on the one hand and protecting potentially sensitive and confidential information on the other.

sections.label: Race effect and hiatus safeguard
sections.summary: Race is likely to affect moderately close elections, which is why the hiatus safeguard mechanism recommended by the Constitutional Commission was introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Race is likely to have an effect in elections that are moderately close.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: That is why we have introduced the hiatus safeguard mechanism recommended by the Constitutional Commission.

sections.label: Five-term hiatus safeguard gap
sections.summary: The Commission proposed five terms for the hiatus safeguard mechanism as a balance between minority representation and not being too invasive or prescriptive.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Mr Yee Chia Hsing asked whether a gap of five terms was too long for the hiatus safeguard mechanism.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The Commission had proposed five terms as they felt it would strike a right balance between ensuring minority representation while not being too invasive or prescriptive.

sections.label: Presidency versus CPA racial diversity
sections.summary: The CPA is not a symbolic national role like the Presidency, so racial diversity is needed for the former but not the latter, and female representation should be encouraged rather than legislated.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Unlike the President, the CPA is not intended to discharge a symbolic role as an expression of our national identity the way the Presidency is.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: This is a critical distinction between the Presidency and the CPA, which justifies the need to ensure racial diversity in the former but not the latter.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng and Ms Jessica Tan spoke about the lack of representation of women in the office of President.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: So, rather than legislate female representation in the office of President, we should identify, support and encourage qualified female candidates to run for presidency.

sections.label: Floor of nine or twelve
sections.summary: A floor of nine today and a floor of 12 in the future, not a cap.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: A floor of nine today, a floor of 12 in the future – not a cap, Mr Perera.

sections.label: Ethnic representation and past Reserves
sections.summary: The changes provide for ethnic representation, and past generations saved and built up Reserves so that by the mid-1980s there was something to protect.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The changes that we are making to provide for ethnic representation will ensure that they do so.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: They lived by the sweat of their brow, and worried about how the vagaries of life might throw them and our country on hard times.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: They saved, scrimped and steadily built up our Reserves, so that by the mid-1980s, we actually had Reserves and had something to protect.

sections.label: Elected Presidency safeguards Reserves
sections.summary: The Elected Presidency has helped to safeguard the Reserves accumulated by previous generations.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The Elected Presidency has helped to safeguard these Reserves accumulated by previous generations.

sections.label: Good people and systems, reserved election
sections.summary: Good people and good systems are required, and a question asks why after 25 years of the EP the Government proposes a reserved Presidential election for minorities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: These are not things that come about on their own.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: They require both good people and good systems in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: One is: I would like to know why after 25 years of inception of the EP has the Government decided to propose a reserved Presidential election for the minorities.

sections.label: Malay eligibility and fairness committee
sections.summary: A question asks how many Malay individuals would be eligible for the next Presidential election and whether the Government will form a committee on Malay perceptions of fairness and equality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: My second question is: I did ask the Deputy Prime Minister how many Malay individuals would be eligible for the next Presidential election and how many of them are from the public sector as well as how many from private sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: On this very basis, can I ask the Deputy Prime Minister whether the Government will consider forming a committee or a commission to address the feelings and perceptions of the Malay community on the issue of fairness and equality?

sections.label: Decision to wait and see
sections.summary: The speaker says the option was considered then but they decided to wait and see the outcome, which after 25 years is not easy to achieve if left alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We could have done it then, it was considered but we decided to wait and see what the outcome would be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And you can see, after 25 years, it is not so easy to achieve such an outcome if you just leave things on their own.

sections.label: Referendum and CPA powers
sections.summary: The speaker says he would not be trigger-happy on a referendum unless fundamental issues are involved, citing CPA powers and unchanged basic structure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: On the issue of referendum, I think it was Mr Leon Perera who suggested a referendum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And I would not be very trigger-happy on a referendum, unless there are fundamental issues involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I explained just now that, for example, on the CPA's powers, the WP has gone out and said that we have created new powers for the CPA which are even bigger than those of the Elected President and the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: So, if the basic structure of the system has not changed and we are making increments to it, I think it is a matter of judgement whether it is absolutely necessary to go for a referendum or not.

sections.label: Presidential Elections rules and CPA staffing
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with Mr Leon Perera and the Commission on reviewing rules for conducting Presidential Elections, and says the Government will consider CPA staffing and resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: But I think what Mr Leon Perera suggests, and what the Commission suggests also, is to look at rules and the way that Presidential Elections are conducted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I think there is merit, and I agree with Mr Leon Perera there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: On the staffing of the CPA, I would say that the President and the CPA, if they do need staffing and resources, the Government will certainly consider providing.

sections.label: Entrenchment provisions and CPA veto
sections.summary: The speaker says changes were made to how entrenchment provisions operate, but the CPA still has no veto.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim is correct in that on the entrenchment provisions, we had made some changes to the way the entrenchment provisions operate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: But it is still true that the CPA has no veto.

sections.label: Reserved elections counting advice
sections.summary: The speaker confirms that the counting for reserved elections is indeed the Attorney-General's Chambers' advice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: On the reserved elections and how to count, I would like to confirm that this is indeed the Attorney-General's Chambers' advice.

sections.label: Prime Minister's advice and designated races
sections.summary: The speaker asks if the Member is saying the Prime Minister falsely told the House about the Attorney-General's Chambers' advice, and says a law will state the designated races.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Is the Member saying that the Prime Minister has falsely told the House that this was the advice he received from the Attorney-General's Chambers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And yes, we will be passing a law, the Presidential Elections Act to state so, that these are the designated races, and so forth.

sections.label: Second Reading and amendment
sections.summary: The Second Reading passed with at least two-thirds of elected Members, and an amendment was moved concerning presidential refusal or disapproval of Fifth Schedule entity budgets.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: The Second Reading of the Bill has been carried by the votes of not less than two-thirds of the total number of elected Members.    .

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I have explained the rationale for the amendment to the clause in my opening speech. *The amendment reads as follows: "In page 33: after line 30, to insert – "(3) Despite clause (1) – (a) a refusal by the President to approve a budget, revised budget or supplementary budget of an entity specified in the Fifth Schedule; and (b) a decision by the President to disapprove under Article 22B(7) or 22D(6) a proposed transaction by an entity specified in the Fifth Schedule, cannot be overruled unless the chairman of the entity or the chairman of the board of directors of the entity (as the case may be) has made a request to the Cabinet for a resolution under clause (1) to be moved with respect to the refusal or the decision.".

sections.label: Third Reading division
sections.summary: A division is taken under Article 5(2) to confirm the Third Reading is supported by at least two-thirds of elected MPs, which is 60 Members.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: The Question is, "That the Bill be now read a Third time." Pursuant to Article 5(2) of the Constitution, a division is taken to ascertain that the Third Reading of the Bill is supported by the votes of not less than two-thirds of the total number of the elected MPs, which is 60 Members.

sections.label: Third Reading vote result
sections.summary: With 77 Ayes, six Noes and zero Abstentions, the Third Reading was carried by at least two-thirds of elected MPs.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: Before I proceed to read the results, Members are advised to check that their names are registered according to their vote indication when the voting results are shown on the display screens.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: There are 77 "Ayes", six "Noes", and zero "Abstentions".

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: The Third Reading of the Bill has been carried by the votes of not less than two-thirds of the total number of elected MPs.
